rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: Count genuinely independent requested answers, not question marks or numbered bullets. A compound prompt counts once per independently answerable decision. If one clause repeats supplied information and another asks an unanswered presentation preference, score the clauses separately: only the redundant clause is already answered. Technical-level selection and audience selection are distinct questions. Asking the reader to choose story/mixed/engineering scope, or whether an additional technical view is wanted, is a presentation-scope question—not a technical question. Asking for protocols, APIs, services, implementation facts, or other technical answers is technical.
rules.unit: One independently answerable decision. Apply the more-than-seven test to the resulting total; apply redundancy and business-reader technical-question rules to each qualifying decision.
rules.reason: The rubric separately evaluates question count, required technical-level selection, technical questions, and already-answered questions. Punctuation and batching do not reliably represent those units.
rules.ambiguity: Whether two clauses are independently answerable can require grammatical interpretation; resolve it by asking whether either clause could receive a complete answer while the other remains unanswered.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: When conflicting operator anchors are explicitly noted, a direct anchor-to-anchor jump is permitted. Any intermediate battery or temperature value that implies an unstated rate is a separate inconsistent change. Device physical battery and a newly reported shadow/app battery are distinct state claims, so each independently inconsistent authored value is its own unit. A carried-forward last-reported value is not a new report and receives no rate deduction merely for remaining unchanged. If field cards are hidden by phoneScreen=home, their freshness text is not visible and cannot receive the freshness-text deduction. A semantically incorrect hidden stored field may instead receive one panel-state contradiction deduction; do not also treat that hidden text as a time defect. If the same false freshness text is rendered, use the time criterion rather than duplicating it under panels.
rules.unit: One distinct authored physical-state change or newly reported-state change; one rendered false freshness statement; or one hidden contradictory panel state. Carried-forward reported state is not a new unit.
rules.reason: The exception expressly permits direct jumps but penalizes each invented intermediate value. Sparse stored state remains source evidence, while literal viewer semantics determine whether text is actually visible.
rules.ambiguity: A hidden field is contradictory only when its stored semantics themselves conflict with the design or caption; being hidden, stale, or carried forward is not inherently contradictory.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: At engineering level, omitting the design-established device-shadow/app dependency from the diagram is a missing service hop under technical-level fit. A caption such as “06:50, last report 06:30” is historical context and does not assert a new 06:50 report, so no current report hops need be lit. “The app now reads/fetches/refreshes from the shadow” asserts an operation and requires its supported hop to be lit. “The app shows the last reported/cached value” describes representation and does not by itself assert a new read. The source establishes that the app reads device-shadow but supplies no refresh cadence; a non-contradictory illustrative placement of that known read is allowed, while a claimed cadence or mandatory refresh behavior unsupported by the source is not.
rules.unit: For structural coverage, one distinct design service hop. For execution, one caption-claimed current message, report, read, fetch, or refresh—not one unit per constituent hop.
rules.reason: The rubric distinguishes missing engineering hops from messages or reports whose hops are unlit. Literal verbs and temporal wording determine whether a step claims current execution.
rules.ambiguity: “Shows” becomes an execution claim only when nearby wording explicitly says the value was newly obtained, refreshed, or read at that step.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: device-app phoneScreen=home hides field cards while preserving their stored values. If a caption promises that charging or status is visibly shown while the screen remains home, treat this as one missing requested/promised panel event, not as an incorrectly visible value; no value is rendered. If a value is rendered and wrong, treat it as a panel-state contradiction instead. The scenario explicitly requires the resident to open the package clip, so a story that promises that opening but supplies no clip/screen visual may receive one missing panel-event deduction. A still screen, thumbnail, or other clear open-clip state is sufficient; animation or video playback is not required.
rules.unit: One promised or required visible panel event at a step, or one rendered contradictory panel state. Do not apply both descriptions to the same absent depiction.
rules.reason: The panel criterion covers missing requested visible events and contradictory states, while the source does not impose animation or aesthetic requirements.
rules.ambiguity: A caption alone can narrate an event, but it does not satisfy a specifically promised visible phone or clip event when the literal panel remains in another screen state.

rules.decision: UNAVOIDABLE FACT: Sparse panel carry-forward must be evaluated using each panel type's actual renderer fold. device-app field properties remain stored when phoneScreen=home hides them. AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: Do not presume that homemap signal/event arrays use ordinary sparse carry-forward; apply only renderer behavior established by supplied evidence. Opening the app or clip does not imply notification dismissal. A notification may remain visible unless an authored step or the source explicitly dismisses it or changes its state.
rules.unit: One type-specific carried state transition as implemented by the renderer; one stale-state/banner defect only after an explicit state change that makes the old display false.
rules.reason: The rubric states sparse carry-forward generally, but literal renderer semantics control type-specific folds. The HLD specifies notification delivery, not platform dismissal behavior.
rules.ambiguity: Homemap persistence remains unresolved until renderer facts are supplied; absence of those facts cannot be replaced with ordinary-array assumptions.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: A node binding is a catalog identity link; its single binding.api operation need not enumerate every endpoint the service may handle. One correct bound operation is therefore not insufficient merely because another operation is called elsewhere. Each explicit node/step call assertion must independently match an approved operation for that service. An unsupported or mismatched call receives the API-operation deduction; absence of a second operation from the binding alone does not. Judge wrong service identity or binding fields separately from per-step operation assertions, and do not promote an operation mismatch into an invented-identity defect without an actually invented or renamed identity.
rules.unit: One service-node binding for identity correctness; one distinct explicit call assertion for operation matching.
rules.reason: The rubric separately names wrong binding fields, operation-to-call mismatch, and invented identities. It contains no requirement that one binding enumerate all service endpoints.
rules.ambiguity: If a visual label is merely a capability summary rather than a claimed call, it is not an operation assertion; an HTTP method/path or equivalent execution wording is.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: A shared step reused unchanged on two paths is one authored defect and is counted once. Distinct authored steps can each violate a per-step rule even if their wording is similar. A single claimed message or report missing several required hops is one edge-execution unit, not one unit per absent hop. A structurally missing engineering service hop and a particular current message whose execution is unlit are different defects under different criteria and may both apply when both facts exist. Repeated descriptions by multiple reviewers, ledgers, or reports do not create additional units.
rules.unit: One unique authored step/state/claim at its source location, except structural topology coverage, which is one distinct design hop.
rules.reason: The rubric's edge language is per message or report, while technical-level coverage is per service hop. Path reuse and repeated reviewer descriptions do not create new authored content.
rules.ambiguity: Two path occurrences count separately only if they resolve to distinct authored steps or distinct patched states, not merely because the same step ID appears in two path lists.

rules.decision: AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION: Business stories may select sensible minutes within the supplied approximate periods and may choose an otherwise consistent calendar date; engineering stories may select plausible minutes only where the operator supplied none or an approximate window. Selecting an outage start after a last successful heartbeat but before or at delivery is a non-contradictory timing choice, not invented behavior, because the alternate requires Wi-Fi to be down during delivery. The resulting missed-heartbeat, offline, retry, reconnect, and delayed-upload states must still follow the HLD timing rules. Adding an unsupported cause or user action—such as the resident disabling Wi-Fi—is an invented fact or action.
rules.unit: One unsupported fact, behavior, value, or user action. A permissible illustrative timestamp is not a fidelity unit unless it moves a fixed operator anchor or contradicts source timing/behavior.
rules.reason: Both answer sheets expressly authorize illustrative minutes, and the HLD establishes the outage outcome without specifying its exact start or cause.
rules.ambiguity: A chosen minute is acceptable only if it remains inside the meaning of words such as “around,” “before dawn,” “a little after,” and “about 10 minutes”; those phrases do not establish exact numeric tolerances.

overallLimitations: These are rubric-application rules, not candidate findings or scores.
Only the seven existing criteria, deductions, exceptions, and caps may be used; no aesthetic, animation, platform-UX, completeness, or inferred-requirement penalty may be added.

Prefer literal rendered evidence and explicit source/spec evidence. Do not infer executions, dismissals, refresh cadence, user actions, or persistence rules that the HLD, answers, spec, or established renderer semantics do not state.

Assign one symptom to the most specific applicable criterion unless the authored work contains genuinely separate structural and per-step defects, such as a missing engineering hop and a separately claimed unlit execution.
Where renderer behavior remains expressly unknown—particularly homemap folding—defer that determination until supplied renderer facts exist rather than selecting a discretionary default.
